conversation.content: How can I compare the metrics for different periods?

To compare metrics for different periods, you can use the time period control available in the metrics interface. This allows you to select specific time frames such as a day, week, month, or quarter, and the data points on the graphs adjust accordingly. You can also create custom time periods. Additionally, metrics can be viewed for predefined periods like 7, 15, 30, 60, or 90 days. The graphs and aggregate values can be adjusted to reflect the selected time period, enabling you to compare metrics across different time frames effectively.
some example of alerts

Examples of alerts include app-level alerts, worker node alerts, zone alerts, cluster alerts, account alerts, and block storage for VPC alerts. Additionally, presence alerts notify when the number of events or logs exceeds expectations, while absence alerts trigger when the number of events or logs falls below expectations. Alerts can be configured with specific conditions, notification channels, and severity levels to monitor infrastructure, applications, and IBM Cloud services.
weak understanding metrics

Weak understanding metrics refer to the number of individual messages that the assistant did not fully comprehend. To improve weak understanding, analyze the Analytics tab to identify areas for improvement. Use metrics to find patterns or common issues in user interactions. Test alternative approaches by creating different versions of the assistant and compare their performance. Refine the assistant's dialog skill based on the insights gained from the logs and metrics. Regularly monitor and update the assistant to enhance its understanding and effectiveness.
those conversations are monitored?

The previous conversations are monitored to improve how the assistant understands and responds to user requests. The Conversations page provides a history of interactions, allowing you to analyze user inputs, actions, and topics. You can filter and explore specific conversations to identify areas for improvement. This monitoring is part of the process to refine the assistant's performance and training data.
are they billed by the number of turns or per conversation?

The billing is managed per monthly active user per service instance. If a single user interacts with assistants hosted by different service instances that belong to the same plan, each interaction is treated as a separate use. You are billed for the user's interaction with each service instance separately. Therefore, you are billed based on the number of interactions (or monthly active users) rather than the number of turns or per conversation.

Metrics for an individual CDN are provided on the Overview tab of the customer portal for that CDN mapping. Two types of metrics are calculated from the CDN's usage: those that show the metrics over a time period as a graph, and those that are shown as aggregate values.

For metrics that display the change over a period of time as a graph, you can see three line graphs and a pie chart. The three line graphs are: Bandwidth, Hits by Mapping, and Hits by Type. They display the activity daily over the course of your specified timeframe. The graphs for Bandwidth and Hits by Mapping are single-line graphs, whereas the breakdown of Hits by Type shows a line for each of the hit types provided. The pie chart displays a regional breakdown of the bandwidth for a CDN mapping on a percentage basis.

Metrics that are shown for aggregate values include Bandwidth Usage in GB, Total Hits to the CDN Edge server, and the Hit Ratio. Hit Ratio indicates that the percentage of times content is delivered by the Edge server, not through its origin. Hit ratio currently is shown as a function of all your CDN mappings, not just the one being viewed.

By default, both the aggregate numbers and the graphs default to show metrics for the last 30 days, but you can change this through the [IBM Cloud console](https://cloud.ibm.com/). Both categories can display metrics for 7-, 15-, 30-, 60-, or 90-day periods.
